en: The Second Book of Pairs (Dukanipāta), Chapter on the Peerless (Asadisavagga)
5. The Jātaka of Discontent Just as when water is turbid and not clear,
One does not see the shells and snails within;
Just as one cannot see gravel, sand, or schools of fish in turbid water,
so too, when the mind is clouded,
one does not perceive one's own welfare or the welfare of others.
Just as in water that is clear and serene,
one sees the snails and shells,
the gravel, the sand, and the schools of fish.
Thus, when the mind is undisturbed,
one sees both one’s own welfare and the welfare of others.
